subject: English
description: Common synonyms asked in banking and SSC exams

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'OBSTINATE'.
questions.explanation: Obstinate = refusing to change one's view despite good reasons. Synonyms — stubborn, headstrong, dogged, intractable, unyielding. Antonyms — flexible, tractable, pliable, compliant. 'Agreeable' and 'hesitant' do not capture the sense of fixed resistance.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'CANDID'.
questions.explanation: Candid = openly honest, straightforward, outspoken. Synonyms — frank, forthright, blunt, open, sincere, outspoken. Antonyms — dishonest, guarded, evasive. Remember — 'candid camera' captures unposed, natural shots.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'LETHARGIC'.
questions.explanation: Lethargic = sluggish, lacking energy or enthusiasm. Synonyms — sluggish, languid, listless, inert, torpid. Antonyms — energetic, vigorous, alert, active. Related noun — lethargy.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'PROCRASTINATE'.
questions.explanation: Procrastinate = to keep putting something off until later, often out of laziness or fear. Synonyms — delay, defer, postpone, dawdle, stall, temporise. Antonyms — expedite, hurry, hasten. Root from Latin 'pro-' (forward) + 'cras' (tomorrow).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'AFFLUENT'.
questions.explanation: Affluent = having plenty of money; prosperous. Synonyms — wealthy, prosperous, rich, opulent, well-off. Antonyms — poor, destitute, impoverished. Also 'affluence' (noun) = abundance of wealth. Related — 'effluent' is a close-sounding but different word meaning 'flowing out' (usually of waste-water).
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'EPHEMERAL'.
questions.explanation: Ephemeral = lasting for a very short time. Synonyms — short-lived, transient, transitory, fleeting, evanescent, momentary. Antonyms — permanent, lasting, enduring, eternal. Origin — Greek 'ephēmeros' (lasting only a day, as in the 'mayfly').
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: Choose the word most similar in meaning to 'RESILIENT'.
questions.explanation: Resilient = able to recover quickly from difficulty; tough. Synonyms — robust, tough, hardy, adaptable, flexible (in the 'bouncing-back' sense). Antonyms — fragile, weak, brittle, vulnerable. Often used for people, economies and materials alike.
questions.subject: English

questions.stem: The principal was widely admired for her BENEVOLENT attitude towards underprivileged students. Which option is closest in meaning to the highlighted word?
questions.explanation: 'Benevolent' means well-meaning and generous — 'showing great kindness and goodwill' captures this exactly. Option B (deliberately cruel) is the antonym. Option C (suspicious) confuses 'benevolent' with 'malevolent', a common mix-up. Option D (wordy) is entirely unrelated.

questions.stem: The candidate's VERBOSE response during the interview failed to impress the selection panel. Which option is closest in meaning to the highlighted word?

options.option_text: speaking in a clear and concise way
using far more words than needed
tending to use blunt and sharp language

questions.explanation: 'Verbose' means using more words than necessary; 'using far more words than needed' is the correct synonym. Option A (clear and concise) is the antonym. Option D (blunt) is confused with being 'terse', the opposite register entirely.

questions.stem: The ACRIMONIOUS dispute between the two senior officers disrupted the functioning of the entire department. Which option best captures the meaning of the highlighted word?

options.option_text: calm and gentle in all interactions
overly eager to please and impress
filled with bitter and sharp hostility

questions.explanation: 'Acrimonious' describes something that is bitter, angry, and full of resentment — 'filled with bitter and sharp hostility' is accurate. Option A is the antonym. Option B confuses it with 'obsequious'. Candidates often pick Option C (hesitant) by mistaking the root 'acri-' (sharp) for uncertainty.

questions.stem: Despite earning a handsome salary, the retired judge led a FRUGAL lifestyle and donated generously to charity. Which option is closest in meaning to the highlighted word?

options.option_text: deeply concerned with social status only

questions.explanation: 'Frugal' means prudently saving resources; 'careful and economical in expenditure' is the precise match. Option A (spending freely) is the antonym — a common trap as the sentence says he 'donated generously', making A tempting but that refers to charity, not his own spending. Option D (wasteful) is also an antonym.

questions.stem: The PLACID surface of Loktak Lake reflected the surrounding Manipur hills perfectly at dawn. Which option is closest in meaning to the highlighted word?

options.option_text: calm, quiet and undisturbed in nature
loud and turbulent in social settings
prone to sudden anxiety and deep worry
sharp and biting in personal remarks

questions.explanation: 'Placid' means serenely calm and undisturbed — perfectly matched by Option A. Option B (turbulent) is the antonym. Candidates may confuse 'placid' with 'flaccid' (limp/weak) and pick Option C; the Latin root 'placere' (to please/soothe) confirms the correct sense.

questions.stem: The new deputy's OBSEQUIOUS manner towards senior bureaucrats earned him little genuine respect from his own subordinates. Which option is closest in meaning to the highlighted word?

options.option_text: overly compliant and eager to please

questions.explanation: 'Obsequious' means fawning or servile — excessively eager to serve or please. Option A is exact. Option B (defiant) is the antonym. Option D is a common wrong choice because candidates read the sentence's negative framing ('little respect') and assume the word must mean 'virtuous'; that is a context-misread trap. The root 'obsequi' (to comply) seals Option A.

questions.stem: Historians have condemned the PERFIDIOUS conduct of the minister who secretly supplied intelligence to the opposing side during the border talks. Which option is closest in meaning to the highlighted word?

options.option_text: fiercely loyal even under extreme duress
guilty of deliberate betrayal of trust
stubbornly resistant to any outside persuasion

questions.explanation: 'Perfidious' derives from Latin 'perfidia' (faithlessness) and means treacherously deceitful — 'guilty of deliberate betrayal of trust' is the exact match. Option A (fiercely loyal) is the antonym and a deliberate trap given the historical framing. Option D (stubbornly resistant) is confused with 'obdurate'; the context clue 'secretly supplied intelligence' should confirm betrayal, not mere resistance.
